On a hot day, a cold treat can be a fun way to help your  dog cool down. Homemade pupsicle recipes are especially convenient because you control the ingredients, portion size, and added sugar.

The best pupsicles for  dogs are simple. Think dog-safe fruits, vegetables, plain yogurt, pumpkin, or small amounts of cooked meat rather than heavily sweetened human popsicles. Below are six easy recipes you can make at home.

Important: These pupsicles are occasional treats, not complete and balanced meals. Introduce new ingredients gradually, and check with your veterinarian if your dog has diabetes, pancreatitis,  food allergies, kidney disease, or another condition requiring a special diet.

What Is a Pupsicle?

A pupsicle is simply a frozen treat made with dog-friendly ingredients. You can freeze the mixture in silicone molds, ice cube trays, or a dog enrichment toy.

Cooking & Recipes

Unlike human popsicles, homemade dog pupsicles should contain no xylitol, chocolate, grapes, raisins, macadamia nuts, or excessive added sugar.

As a general rule, treats and extras should make up no more than about 10% of your dog’s daily calories.

1. Peanut Butter and Banana Pupsicles

Banana and peanut butter make a creamy frozen treat that many dogs enjoy.

Ingredients

  • 1 ripe banana
  • 1/2 cup plain, unsweetened yogurt
  • 1 tablespoon dog-safe peanut butter
  • 1–2 tablespoons water, if needed
    • Food

Directions

Mash the banana until smooth. Mix in the yogurt and peanut butter. Spoon the mixture into silicone molds and freeze for at least 3–4 hours.

Safety tip: Always check the peanut butter label carefully. It must be xylitol-free (xylitol may also be listed as birch sugar).

Because peanut butter is calorie-dense, keep portions small.

2. Pumpkin and Yogurt Pupsicles

Plain pumpkin works particularly well for dogs that enjoy softer, mildly flavored treats.

Jams, Jellies & Preserves

Ingredients

  • 1/2 cup plain pumpkin puree
  • 1/2 cup plain, unsweetened yogurt
  • 2 tablespoons water

Directions

Mix everything until evenly combined. Pour into molds and freeze until solid.

Use 100% plain pumpkin, not pumpkin pie filling, which may contain sugar and spices.

If your dog enjoys pumpkin, you can also try our [Pumpkin Soup for Dogs] for another simple way to serve it.

3. Blueberry Banana Pupsicles

These colorful pupsicles require only a few ingredients.

Fruits & Vegetables

Ingredients

  • 1/2 ripe banana
  • 1/3 cup blueberries
  • 1/2 cup plain yogurt
  • A little water

Directions

Mash or blend the banana and blueberries. Stir in the yogurt and enough water to reach a spoonable consistency. Transfer to molds and freeze.

You can also leave a few blueberries whole for larger dogs, although crushing them makes the treats easier to portion.

For small dogs and puppies, use small molds to reduce the risk of gulping a large frozen piece.

4. Watermelon Pupsicles for Dogs

Watermelon makes a refreshing pupsicle because of its high water content.

Cooking & Recipes

Ingredients

  • 1 cup seedless watermelon flesh
  • 1/4 cup water

Directions

Remove all rind and seeds. Blend the watermelon flesh with water, pour it into molds, and freeze.

That’s it—no yogurt or sweetener is necessary.

Never freeze pieces of watermelon rind for your dog. The tough rind is difficult to digest and may create a choking or gastrointestinal obstruction risk.

5. Chicken and Carrot Savory Pupsicles

Not every pupsicle needs to be fruity. This savory version is useful for dogs that prefer meat flavors.

Dogs

Ingredients

  • 1/2 cup fully cooked, unseasoned chicken
  • 1/4 cup cooked carrots
  • 1/2 cup water

Directions

Finely chop or blend the cooked chicken and carrots with water. Divide among molds and freeze until firm.

Use boneless, skinless chicken without salt, garlic, onion, sauces, or seasoning.

These treats are richer than fruit-and-water pupsicles, so serve small portions and refrigerate or freeze leftovers promptly during preparation.

6. Cantaloupe Yogurt Pupsicles

Cantaloupe’s natural sweetness makes it an easy summer treat for many dogs.

Fruits & Vegetables

Ingredients

  • 1/2 cup ripe cantaloupe
  • 1/2 cup plain, unsweetened yogurt
  • 1–2 tablespoons water

Directions

Remove the rind and seeds. Blend the cantaloupe flesh with yogurt and a little water. Pour into molds and freeze for several hours.

If your  dog does not tolerate dairy well, skip the yogurt and blend the cantaloupe with water instead.

Quick Pupsicle Recipe Comparison

How Much Pupsicle Can a Dog Have?

Portion size matters even when the ingredients are healthy.

Cooking & Recipes

A small dog may need only a small ice-cube-sized pupsicle, while a large dog can generally handle a larger portion. Start small the first time to see how your dog’s digestive system responds.

Remember to include pupsicle calories when calculating your dog’s overall treat intake. If your dog needs to shed a few pounds, see our guide on [How to Help My Dog Lose Weight] before adding calorie-dense treats regularly.

Can Puppies Have Pupsicles?

Healthy puppies that are already eating solid food can generally have tiny amounts of appropriate dog-safe frozen treats. However, their complete and balanced puppy food should provide nearly all of their nutrition.

Choose soft, appropriately sized pupsicles and supervise your puppy while eating. For more puppy feeding guidance, read [How Often Should Puppies Eat?].

Ingredients to Avoid in Homemade Dog Pupsicles

The fact that something freezes well doesn’t mean it belongs in a dog’s treat. Avoid:

Dogs

  • Xylitol/birch sugar
  • Chocolate or cocoa
  • Grapes and raisins
  • Macadamia nuts
  • Alcohol
  • Coffee or caffeine
  • Onion and garlic
  • Large amounts of sugar
  • Heavily salted ingredients
  • Artificially sweetened human desserts

Also check flavored yogurt, peanut butter, broth, and other packaged ingredients before using them.

How Long Do Homemade Pupsicles Last?

Store pupsicles in a sealed freezer-safe container. For best quality, I recommend making small batches and using them within 2–4 weeks.

Labeling the container with the preparation date makes it easier to keep track.

FAQs

Can dogs eat pupsicles every day?

They don’t need them daily. Pupsicles should be considered treats and included within your dog’s overall calorie allowance.

Biological Sciences

Can I use Greek yogurt?

Yes, plain, unsweetened Greek yogurt can work for dogs that tolerate dairy. Avoid products containing xylitol or lots of added sugar.

Can I use chicken broth?

Only if you carefully check the ingredients. Many human broths contain onion, garlic, or excessive sodium. Plain water is the easiest option.

Can dogs eat frozen fruit?

Many dog-safe fruits can be served frozen in appropriately sized portions. However, avoid toxic fruits such as grapes and raisins.

What can I use if my dog cannot eat dairy?

Use water, mashed banana, plain pumpkin, or an appropriate dog-safe ingredient as the liquid/base instead of yogurt.

Final Thoughts

These homemade pupsicle recipes for dogs provide an easy way to make refreshing treats using ingredients you already recognize. Watermelon pupsicles are great when you want something simple, while chicken and carrot pupsicles offer a savory alternative.

Food

Whichever recipe you choose, keep portions modest, introduce unfamiliar foods gradually, and make sure treats don’t replace your dog’s complete and balanced everyday diet.
